name: Concrete & Kin
description: A long-running serialized neural-feed drama following three generations of a the Gray Zone family navigating debt cycles, augmentation black markets, and the slow erosion of corponation encroachment on Tier 1 territory. Each episode places the viewer inside a different family member's body — a grandmother who remembers the pre-corponation years, her daughter who runs aug repairs out of a flooded basement, and a teenage grandson being recruited by a runner crew. The show is celebrated for its unflinching sensory realism; the hunger, the cold, the weight of chronic debt are fully transmitted.
cultural_impact: Introduced the phrase 'kin-weight' into Meridian vernacular — the specific exhaustion of holding a family together across tiers — which has since entered common speech across all tiers.
story_hooks: A player character discovers their own family history is documented in an episode they were never meant to see
The showrunner resurfaces after years in hiding, claiming to have recorded an episode that names a specific Spire executive by name
A Vantablack enforcement team is hunting the last known physical copy of Season 4, which went underground before digital distribution
